skills.name: Accounting for investment transactions: fixed assets acquired

note.text:
Investment transactions buy fixed assets: items kept and used for more than one year (class 2): 231 Buildings, 241 Equipment, 244 Office furniture and equipment, 245 Transport equipment, 2183 Computer equipment.
Purchase on credit: debit the asset account (HT), debit 4451 VAT recoverable on fixed assets, credit 481 Suppliers of fixed assets (TTC).
Payment by bank: debit 481 Suppliers of fixed assets, credit 521 Bank.
Purchase paid at once: credit 521 Bank (or 571 Cash) directly.
Fixed assets are not expenses: they are recorded in class 2.

sections.heading: Investing in fixed assets
sections.text:
A fixed asset is something the enterprise keeps and uses for more than one year to do its work: buildings, machines, office furniture, computers, vehicles. They are recorded in class {2}, not as expenses.
Paper, ink and fuel, used up quickly, are expenses (class {6}).

sections.heading: The entries
Why a separate supplier account?
sections.text:
{'401 Suppliers'} is for suppliers of goods and services used in daily trading; {'481'} is for suppliers of fixed assets. Keeping them apart shows clearly how much the business owes for investments.
Example: a van at {4000000} FCFA HT: VAT {770000} FCFA, TTC {4770000} FCFA owed to the supplier of fixed assets.

key_words.meaning: an item kept and used for more than a year
account {'481'}: amounts owed for fixed assets bought on credit

mistake.wrong: A delivery van is recorded in {'601'} Purchases of goods
mistake.right: It is a fixed asset: {'245'} Transport equipment
mistake.why: {'601'} is for goods bought to resell; the van is used for years.

worked_example.problem: A business buys a delivery van for {ht} FCFA HT on credit (VAT {19.25}%). Give the entry.
steps: Debit {'245 Transport equipment'} {ht}; debit {'4451 VAT recoverable'} {ht * 0.1925}.

cards.idea: A fixed asset is kept and used for more than a year.
example: A computer, a vehicle, a building

cards.idea: Fixed assets bought on credit: credit Suppliers of fixed assets.
The VAT on fixed assets is recoverable.

check.prompt: Equipment is bought for {ht} FCFA HT (VAT {19.25}%). What amount is credited to {'481'} Suppliers of fixed assets (FCFA)?

misconceptions.explain: The supplier is owed the amount including tax.

pick.q: A photocopier bought for the office, to be used for five years
w: No: it is an expense of the month
No: it is stock for sale
e: Items used for years are capitalised.
It is not bought to resell.
pick.y: Long-term use makes it a fixed asset.

pick.q: Reams of paper used up in a month
A lorry bought by a transport company
w: No: it is a purchase of goods (601)
e: The company uses it, it does not resell it.
pick.y: Used for many years: fixed asset.

pick.q: Office furniture is bought on credit for 500 000 FCFA HT (VAT 96 250).
pick.r: Dr 244 Office furniture 500 000; Dr 4451 VAT 96 250 / Cr 481 Suppliers of fixed assets 596 250
e: Furniture used by the business is a fixed asset, not goods for resale.
It was bought on credit, and the VAT is recorded separately.
pick.y: Asset HT and recoverable VAT debited; supplier of fixed assets credited TTC.

pick.q: The supplier of fixed assets is paid 596 250 FCFA by cheque.
pick.r: Dr 481 Suppliers of fixed assets / Cr 521 Bank
w: Dr 521 Bank / Cr 481 Suppliers of fixed assets
e: Paid by cheque from the bank, to the supplier of fixed assets.
pick.y: The debt falls; the bank falls.

pick.q: A computer is bought and paid at once by bank: 800 000 FCFA HT, VAT 154 000.
pick.r: Dr 2183 Computer equipment 800 000; Dr 4451 VAT 154 000 / Cr 521 Bank 954 000
e: A computer for use is a fixed asset.
It was paid at once by bank, and VAT is separate.

questions.prompt: Equipment is bought for {ht} FCFA HT (VAT {19.25}%). What amount is credited to {'481'} Suppliers of fixed assets (FCFA)?

misconceptions.explain: The supplier is owed the amount including tax.

questions.prompt: During the year a business buys a building for {b} FCFA and a vehicle for {v} FCFA (HT), and pays {r} FCFA to suppliers of fixed assets. If nothing was owed before, how much is still owed to suppliers of fixed assets, including VAT ({19.25}%) (FCFA)?

misconceptions.explain: The suppliers are owed the amounts including VAT.
